newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks end higher, but Wall Street looms.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks end higher, but Wall Street looms.

text.p: Madrid stocks ended higher on Friday, well supported by stronger bonds and pesetas and backed by other European markets, dealers said.
Despite an initial sell-off, Wall Street bounced back and supported the close in European bourses but left dealers wary.

"We had a crazy close tonight. Market volatility is high. People are scared by the U.S. markets," a dealer said, adding that positive hopes on Spain's March consumer price index also supported stocks.
The general index was up 4.45 points, 0.96 percent, at 466.12 and the Ibex-35 gained 56.1 points, 1.06 percent, to 5,336.09.
Dealers said it was difficult to make any forecast in the short run, and they were limiting activity to intra-day trading.
Repsol, which is expected to start on Monday the public offer of the last 10 percent stake still in state hands, gained 20 pesetas to 5,840.
